In the context of estimation problems, rounding procedures for sum-of-squares hierarchies tend to work well if there is a unique target solution (e.g., a planted sparse vector in a random subspace) or if there is a small number of target solutions (e.g., the components of a low-rank tensor). One could try to simplify the structure of the set of separating directions, e.g., by focusing on ”extreme” separating directions of the form v = Σ−1 (µa −µb ). Unfortunately, we do not know the same kind of characterization in terms of polynomial inequalities for such a simplified set of separating directions. 12.
